hook_text: Six apple slices, a pinch of salt and a sunny windowsill. In a week, two of the three plates win.
clip_script: Germs need water. Dry the food and they stop. That is biltong, bokkoms and dried peaches. Salt pulls water out of the food and out of the germs by osmosis, and what stays behind is too salty for them anyway. That is salted snoek and bacon. The test: six equal slices, weighed. Two plain, two salted, two in the sun under a mesh. Same room, weighed every day, looked at every day. Plain ones mould by day four. Salted ones sit in their own brine, firm. Dried ones shrink to leather, nothing grows. Graph the mass. No tasting, ever. The plain plate is not a waste; it is the proof.
visual_style: Whiteboard three plates labelled; a scale reading dropping day by day; mould dots appearing on the control; brine pooling round the salted slice; a shrinking dried slice; a three-line graph.
pacing: Water, dry, salt, osmosis, six slices, daily, three results, graph, control.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and set up your three plates tonight with a scale and a notebook.
